Laura — ran a short pass. High-level findings below; I attached a quick calc tab (internal link) and pasted the core numbers.

Assumptions used (explicit):
- Hosted price (gen text): $0.00030 per output token, $0.00002 per input token (blended list for our curated open models)
- Dedicated effective cost: estimated $0.00012 per token at their expected utilization (after batching/caching benefits)
- Default batch latency allowed: 50ms for evaluation (we tested sensitivity at 20ms and 200ms)
- Cacheable fraction: 38% (from MediServ); we modeled 0% / 25% / 50%
- Completion tail risk: +2x tokens in P95 case

Key results (rounded):
- P50 tokens/session: 420 tokens -> Hosted cost/session ≈ $0.13; Dedicated cost/session ≈ $0.05
- P95 scenario (+2x completion): 840 tokens -> Hosted ≈ $0.25; Dedicated ≈ $0.10

Sensitivity to caching (P50, hosted):
- 0% cacheable -> $0.16/session
- 25% cacheable -> $0.12/session
- 50% cacheable -> $0.09/session

Batching impact (tokens/$ improvement vs no batching at 20ms/50ms/200ms):
- 20ms: +6% efficiency (better kernel utilization)
- 50ms: +9% (baseline we recommend)
- 200ms: +15% efficiency but latency likely noticeable; only recommended for background bulk jobs

Autoscaling note: 90 concurrent sessions with 300 active pilot users will push Hosted into mid-tier concurrency where burst capacity pricing increments matter. If MediServ wants a hard SLA for latency we should propose a small Dedicated pool (~2-4 GPUs depending on model family) — that narrows tokens/$ variance and gives predictable tail costs.

Action items I did:
- Uploaded calc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz-MAP-templates (internal)
- One-pager summary drafted — see tab ‘MAP_unit_econ_summary’

I’ll be available to review the slide with Pricing Thursday morning. If you want me to replace the blended hosted numbers with a specific model SKU, call it out and I’ll recompute.

— Karthik
